Does anyone out there have any good methods to run a local sandbox or otherwise some way to persistently develop your custom CSS without say, using an arbitrary test sub or rolling a local voat server? The only ways I can think to play around are by using the browser tools or Firebug (which I don't think I can make persistent) or to spend some time whipping up a mock-up of a sub's front page with matching CSS for me to manipulate. I am missing something simple? Is there some clever way to accomplish this?

I see I can copy/paste to/from Firebug's CSS tab, but this seems a little ham-fisted.

This may not be the best method, but I'll let you know how I do it in my Firefox:

Firstly, I load up my Firefox and Sublime Text (a text editor). I have Firebug and Web Developer as Firefox addons. In Sublime Text, I load up a new file for the CSS [A] (yes, I still need to pay for it).

In Firebug, I start making changes [B] to the subverse CSS and manually record them into Sublime Text. [C] I then save the CSS file [D] from Sublime Text.

On the Web Developer toolbar, I go to CSS > Add User Style Sheet... [E] then select my CSS file.

In this way, I make quick tweaks in my browser while recording permanent changes to Sublime Text. Every now and again, I re-add the CSS file to update my longterm changes. I do this until I have a finished theme.

That's the closest I get to a sandbox as you describe.
